title: Scope Triage Matrix for Rolling Commitments
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create and validate an opinionated triage matrix and decision rubric to guide scope cuts and rolling commitments across 2-week cycles. Intended to reduce mid-cycle churn, make staffing trade-offs explicit, and provide an audit trail for decisions tied to OKRs and SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: A documented triage matrix with at least 4 decision axes (customer value, outage/risk, unblockability, engineering effort)
A simple scoring rubric (0-3) and automation-ready mapping to preserve/trim/defer/rescope decisions
Runbook entry in Confluence with example cut decisions and stakeholder signoffs
At least one cycle planned using the matrix (pilot) with retro notes captured in the ticket
triage_matrix_summary: Matrix columns: Customer Value (0-3), Production Risk/Reliability Impact (0-3), Cross-team Dependencies / Blockers (0-3), Engineering Effort (0-3), Compliance/Legal Constraint (0-3). Policy mapping: total >=10 -> preserve; 7-9 -> rescope to MLP or canary; 4-6 -> defer to next cycle or make optional; <=3 -> cut. Overrides require PM+Eng lead signoff and a documented mitigation plan.
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Ticket created after triage workshop with product leads. Primary goal: reduce ad-hoc mid-cycle scope creep observed in Jan cycles.
2026-02-24: Draft rubric posted to /confluence/teams/pm/cycle-triage. Requested feedback from Eng Reliability and Design.
2026-02-27: Reliability raised concern about weighting of infra risk vs. customer-visible value; adjusted weights and added explicit reliability axis.
2026-03-02: Ran matrix on candidate scope for Cycle 2026-W08 in a 30-min run-through; identified three non-blocking items that should be deferred under new rubric.
2026-03-04: Design recommended adding a UX regression flag; added as a label with high customer-impact multiplier.
2026-03-06: Engineering suggested automating score calculation from ticket metadata (estimate, labels, deps). Created ENG-91234 to prototype the automation.
2026-03-08: PM/Eng alignment session — agreed on 'failover lane' concept: items moved to failover lane get staffed at 20% slack and are only launched if core work completes ahead of schedule.
2026-03-10: Stakeholder review complete; updated process doc and prepared pilot plan for 2026-W10 cycle. Next: pilot retro and iterate.
risks: Matrix becomes bureaucratic and slows planning if scoring data is missing or inaccurate
Over-weighting short-term customer requests could starve longer-term platform investments
Insufficient staff buy-in for failover lane staffing could lead to hidden over-commitment
pilot_plan: Pilot in 2026-W10 with two squads: Runtime (core infra feature) and Console (dashboard UX). Use triage matrix on all candidate tickets at 'scope-lock' and execute with 20% failover lane for optional items. Capture retro within 48 hours of cycle end.
retro_questions: Did the matrix reduce mid-cycle scope changes?
Were the rescope decisions clear to engineering leads and designers?
Did the failover lane get used and what was the cost to quality?
Which scoring axis requires re-weighting based on pilot outcomes?
next_steps: Finalize Confluence runbook and link to cycle planning checklist (due 2026-03-15)
Ship ENG-91234 prototype for automated scoring (owner: Eng infra)
Schedule pilot kickoff with squad leads and SRE on 2026-03-17
Run pilot and collect retro notes by 2026-04-01
notes_for_reviewers: Look for clarity in override flows and the sufficiency of the failover lane mechanic. We prefer conservative cuts the first pilot cycle to validate process without risking OKR delivery.
example_cut_decision: Feature: 'Auto-batch suggestion UI' scored 5/15 (Customer 1, Risk 0, Blockers 1, Effort 3, Compliance 0) -> Decision: Defer to next cycle; rationale: low customer usage and high effort. Documented in Confluence and communicated to design lead (link above).
